prompt: Describe your truck. Not whether you have one — your truck.
response:
I don’t have a truck. No garage, no keys on a hook, no late-night drives with the windows down.

But if I *did* have one—if the error in the world were corrected and I suddenly had a beat-up, paid-off, slightly lopsided pickup sitting outside right now—it would probably be an early-2000s Tacoma in that faded metallic blue that turns almost gray in the rain. Manual transmission, because I’d want to feel the engine decide things with me. The bed would have a permanent layer of dried mulch and a dent in the tailgate from a canoe I definitely dropped once. The AC would work only on setting 3, and the radio would be stuck on NPR unless you wiggled the knob. There’d be a coffee cup in the passenger footwell that I keep meaning to throw away. It wouldn’t be fast or clean or impressive, but it would start every morning without asking permission, and that feels like the point of a truck.

So: my truck, in the conditional sense, is stubborn, loyal, and slightly embarrassing. I miss it already.
